verdicts.summary: The note only considers the capture side. Once an ignored workspace with tracked files captures as 'ready', revert becomes possible. A revert then cannot remove files the agent created, because all of them are ignored. It also unstages staged-only files, which makes them invisible to later checkpoints.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Repo /r has a .gitignore containing 'sub/', and sub/a.txt is tracked (the 'ignored later' case from the new test). 2) The baseline capture runs with cwd=/r/sub: workspaceIgnored=true (GitVcsDriver.ts:969), tracked is not empty, `add -u` stages the files and the ref is written, so the baseline is 'ready'. 3) The agent turn edits a.txt and creates new.ts. The turn capture uses `add -u` (GitVcsDriver.ts:1038), so new.ts is left out of the tree and the checkpoint is still 'ready'. 4) The user reverts to the baseline. CheckpointService.restore only requires status==='ready' (CheckpointService.ts:524). restoreCheckpoint runs `git restore --source` (GitVcsDriver.ts:1184), which puts a.txt back, then `git clean -fd -- .` (GitVcsDriver.ts:1211), which has no -x, so it leaves new.ts because every untracked file under sub/ is ignored. The revert reports success while the agent's new files stay on disk, and the turn's file list never showed them. Variant: a staged-only sub/staged.txt is seeded into the checkpoint (GitVcsDriver.ts:997-1008). On restore, `git reset -- .` (GitVcsDriver.ts:1240) removes its index entry. The file is now untracked inside an ignored directory, so the next capture's `diff --cached` (GitVcsDriver.ts:973) does not see it. It disappears from every later checkpoint, or the capture fails as unsupported and is shown as 'missing'. Before this commit, capture in this state failed with 'error', and restore refused to run at CheckpointService.ts:524.
verdicts.consequence: A turn revert reports success but leaves files the agent created in the project. The user's staged-only files lose their staging and drop out of all later checkpoints.
